Select the notes and, if known, the lowest sounding note. Repeated notes in different octaves do not add new pitch classes, but the bass and spacing still matter. E–G–C with E lowest can be C/E: a C major chord in first inversion.

Select each different note on the keyboard above. For example, choose C, E and G to look for a C major chord. Select a key again to remove it.

If you know the lowest note, choose it under Lowest note. Otherwise leave Bass not specified. The keyboard records note names, not octaves or repeated notes, so it cannot recover the original spacing of the chord.
